literal: " Ting had also heard his words clearly; because the empress had no favor, he reported the slanderous verse to the emperor, saying, "A hundred pints fly up to heaven; bright moon shines on Chang'an.
idiomatic: " Zu Ting had heard him plainly enough. With the empress out of favor, he carried the verse to the emperor: "A hundred pints fly up to heaven; bright moon shines on Chang'an.

literal: " He had his wife's elder brother Zheng Daogai memorialize it.
idiomatic: " He had his wife's elder brother Zheng Daogai submit the accusation.

literal: The emperor questioned Ting; Ting confirmed it.
idiomatic: The emperor questioned Zu Ting, and Ting swore it was true.

literal: He also spoke of a verse: "The high mountain collapses; the oak tree rises; a blind old man carries a great axe on his back; a meddlesome old woman cannot speak.
idiomatic: He added another verse: "The high mountain collapses; the oak tree rises; a blind old man carries a great axe on his back; a meddlesome old woman cannot speak.

literal: " Ting also said that "the blind old man" was himself, that he shared the state's joy and sorrow, and urged the emperor to act; he said that "the meddlesome old woman" resembled Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu of the Way.
idiomatic: " He said "the blind old man" meant himself — one who shared the state's weal and woe — and pressed the emperor to move. "The meddlesome old woman," he said, was Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu of the Way.

literal: The emperor asked Han Changluan and Mu Tipo, and also ordered Gao Yuanhai and Duan Shiliang to deliberate on it in secret; the group would not agree.
idiomatic: The emperor consulted Han Changluan and Mu Tipo and secretly ordered Gao Yuanhai and Duan Shiliang to weigh the matter; none of them would go along.

literal: Thereupon, through staff officer Feng Shirang of Guang's office, a memorial reported that Guang was rebelling, and his clan was destroyed.
idiomatic: Then Feng Shirang, a staff officer in Guang's headquarters, memorialized that Guang was plotting rebellion, and the whole clan was wiped out.

literal: Ting again attached himself to Lu Matron and asked to be made commander of the guards; the Later Sovereign assented.
idiomatic: Ting courted Lu Matron again and asked for command of the guards; the Later Sovereign agreed.

literal: The edict required a confirming memorial; the signature of Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaqing was to be obtained.
idiomatic: The edict had to be confirmed by memorial, with the signature of attendant-in-ordinary Hulu Xiaqing.

literal: Xiaqing secretly told Gao Yuanhai; Yuanhai said to Hou Lü Fen and Mu Tipo, "Xiaozheng is a Han fellow, and both his eyes cannot even see things — how could he be fit to command the guards?
idiomatic: Xiaqing secretly warned Gao Yuanhai. Yuanhai told Hou Lü Fen and Mu Tipo, "Xiaozheng is a Han man, and his eyes can barely make out a thing — how is he fit to command the guards?

literal: " The next morning he memorialized in person, fully stating Ting's unfitness, and also wrote that Ting was intimate with Prince of Guangning Xiaohang, with none of a great minister's bearing.
idiomatic: " Next morning he spoke to the throne in person, listing every reason Ting was unfit, and charged that Ting was thick with Prince of Guangning Xiaohang and lacked a minister's dignity.

literal: Ting also asked for a face-to-face audience; the emperor ordered him brought in.
idiomatic: Ting demanded an audience; the emperor had him admitted.

literal: Ting offered his own defense and also said that he and Yuanhai had long disliked each other — Yuanhai must be the one slandering him.
idiomatic: Ting pleaded his case and said Yuanhai had always hated him — this accusation could only be Yuanhai's slander.

literal: The emperor's face went slack and he could not deny it; he said, "So it is.
idiomatic: The emperor flushed and could not deny it. "True," he said.

literal: " Ting listed Yuanhai together with Director of the Granaries Yin Zihua, Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse Li Shuyuan, Director of Market Regulation Zhang Shulüe, and others as forming factions and building cliques.
idiomatic: " Ting named Yuanhai, director of the granaries Yin Zihua, vice director of the imperial storehouse Li Shuyuan, director of market regulation Zhang Shulüe, and others as men who formed factions and built cliques.

literal: Thereupon Zihua was made governor of Renzhou, Shuyuan governor of Xiangcheng commandery, and Shulüe recorder of the headquarters staff in Southern Camp Province.
idiomatic: Zihua was sent out as governor of Renzhou, Shuyuan as governor of Xiangcheng commandery, and Shulüe as headquarters recorder in Southern Camp Province.

literal: Lu Matron chimed in as well, and Yuanhai was again made governor of Zhengzhou.
idiomatic: Lu Matron joined the chorus, and Yuanhai was packed off as governor of Zhengzhou.

literal: From this Ting alone held the levers of power and oversaw all cavalry and external military affairs.
idiomatic: From then on Ting alone held the levers of state and directed every matter of cavalry and field armies.

literal: Kinsmen within and without all won eminent posts.
idiomatic: Kinsmen inside and outside the court all won eminent posts.

literal: The Later Sovereign also had several inner attendants support him in and out; he wore a gauze cap all the way to the Eternal Lane, went out the Wanchun Gate toward the Hall of Sacred Longevity, and each day shared the imperial couch to decide government — such trust in his commission no minister could match.
idiomatic: The Later Sovereign had several inner attendants steady him coming and going. He wore a gauze cap through the Eternal Lane, out the Wanchun Gate to the Hall of Sacred Longevity, and daily shared the imperial couch to settle affairs — a commission no minister could rival.

literal: Since He Shikai had held power, the body politic had rotted; Ting exalted men of high repute, made officials fit their posts, and won praise within and without.
idiomatic: Since He Shikai's tenure the body politic had rotted. Ting exalted men of standing, put officials in posts that suited them, and won praise at court and beyond.

literal: He again wished to add and cut in government affairs and to sift out personnel.
idiomatic: He again meant to trim government and sift the ranks.

literal: At first he memorialized to abolish the Capital Region office and merge it into the guards; matters touching the common people would all return to the commanderies and counties.
idiomatic: First he memorialized to abolish the Capital Region office and fold it into the guards, returning every matter that touched common people to the commanderies and counties.

literal: Titles such as commander of the night guard would follow the old official names; civil and military insignia and dress would all follow precedent.
idiomatic: Titles like commander of the night guard would revert to older names; civil and military insignia and dress would follow precedent.

literal: He also wished to dismiss the various eunuchs and petty men, extend sincerity and summon scholars — a plan for bringing order.
idiomatic: He also meant to dismiss the eunuchs and petty favorites, extend sincerity, and summon scholars — his recipe for order.

literal: Lu Matron and Mu Tipo debated with considerable disagreement.
idiomatic: Lu Matron and Mu Tipo argued on opposite sides.

literal: Ting therefore prompted Vice Director of the Censorate Li Boju to impeach Chief Clerk Wang Zichong for taking bribes, knowing the case would implicate Mu Tipo; he wished guilt by bribery to spread, hoping thereby to bring them down together with Lu Matron.
idiomatic: Ting therefore nudged vice director of the censorate Li Boju to impeach chief clerk Wang Zichong for bribery, knowing the case would rope in Mu Tipo — he meant the taint of graft to spread and pull Lu Matron down with them.

literal: Still fearing the Later Sovereign was drowning in his intimates, he wished to gain support through the empress's faction; he asked that the empress's elder brother Hu Junyu be made attendant-in-ordinary and central commander of the guards, and also summoned Junyu's elder brother Junbi, governor of Liang Province, intending to make him vice director of the censorate.
idiomatic: Still fearing the Later Sovereign was drowning in favorites, he sought backing from the empress's kin: he asked that her elder brother Hu Junyu be made attendant-in-ordinary and central commander of the guards, and summoned Junyu's brother Junbi, governor of Liang Province, intending to make him vice director of the censorate.

literal: Lu Matron heard and nursed anger; by every means she slandered and destroyed them; Junyu was at once sent out as Bearer of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, relieved of central command of the guards, and Junbi returned to his post in Liang Province.
idiomatic: Lu Matron heard and burned with anger. She slandered them by every means, had Junyu made bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon and stripped of the guards, and sent Junbi back to Liang Province.

literal: The empress's deposition owed much to this as well.
idiomatic: The empress's deposition owed much to this as well.

literal: Wang Zichong was released without inquiry.
idiomatic: Wang Zichong was released without inquiry.

literal: Ting grew daily more distant.
idiomatic: Ting grew more distant by the day.

literal: The eunuchs again joined in slandering him, to every extreme.
idiomatic: The eunuchs again joined in slandering him, to every extreme.

literal: The Later Sovereign questioned Tai Ji; she grieved in silence and would not answer; after three questions she left the couch and bowed, saying, "This old serving-woman deserves death. I saw He Shikai say that Xiaozheng was broadly learned and talented and called him a good man, and so I recommended him.
idiomatic: The Later Sovereign questioned Tai Ji. She grieved in silence until he asked a third time; then she left the couch and bowed. "This old serving-woman deserves death," she said. "He Shikai told me Xiaozheng was learned and gifted and a good man, and so I raised him up.

literal: Watching him lately, he is nothing but guilt — men are hard to know.
idiomatic: Watching him now, he is nothing but guilt — men are hard to know.

literal: This old serving-woman deserves death.
idiomatic: This old serving-woman deserves death.

literal: " The Later Sovereign ordered Han Changluan to investigate the case; more than ten matters were found in which he had forged edicts to receive gifts; because of an earlier heavy oath not to kill him, Ting was relieved of attendant-in-ordinary and vice director, and sent out as governor of Northern Xuzhou.
idiomatic: " The Later Sovereign ordered Han Changluan to investigate. They found more than ten cases of forged edicts and illicit gifts. Because of an earlier solemn oath not to kill him, Ting was stripped of attendant-in-ordinary and vice director and sent out as governor of Northern Xuzhou.

literal: Ting asked to see the Later Sovereign; Han Changluan, who had long resented Ting, sent men to push him out of the Cypress Pavilion.
idiomatic: Ting begged an audience with the Later Sovereign. Han Changluan, who had long hated him, sent men to thrust him from the Cypress Pavilion.

literal: Ting insisted on a face-to-face audience and sat, refusing to move.
idiomatic: Ting insisted on seeing him face to face and sat, refusing to budge.

literal: Changluan then ordered soldiers to drag him out, set Ting in the court hall, and reviled him severely.
idiomatic: Changluan ordered soldiers to drag him out, set him in the court hall, and reviled him without mercy.

literal: After he had set out on the road, an order recalled him, stripped his open office and state equal to the Three Excellencies and his commandery dukehood, and left him a plain governor.
idiomatic: After he had set out, an order recalled him, stripped his open office, state equal to the Three Excellencies, and commandery dukedom, and left him a plain governor.

literal: On reaching the province, Chen raiders appeared and many of the people rebelled.
idiomatic: On reaching his province, Chen raiders struck and much of the populace rose against him.

literal: Ting did not close the city gates; he ordered the men on the ramparts to leave the walls and sit in silence; streets were barred to travelers; chickens and dogs were forbidden to cry.
idiomatic: Ting did not shut the gates. He ordered the rampart guards down to sit in silence, barred the streets to foot traffic, and forbade chickens and dogs to make a sound.

literal: The bandits heard and saw nothing, could not fathom the reason, grew doubtful as men fled and the city stood empty, and set no watch.
idiomatic: The bandits heard and saw nothing, could not guess his design, took fright as men fled and the city seemed empty, and posted no watch.

literal: Ting suddenly ordered a great shout; drums and clamor shook heaven; the bandits were greatly alarmed and at once scattered.
idiomatic: Ting suddenly ordered a great shout; drums and clamor shook the sky; the bandits panicked and scattered at once.

literal: Later they again formed ranks and advanced on the city; Ting rode out himself, ordered recorder Wang Junzhi to lead horse and foot, and still personally went into the fight.
idiomatic: Later they formed ranks and marched on the city again. Ting rode out himself, ordered recorder Wang Junzhi to lead horse and foot, and still fought in the front line.

literal: The bandits had earlier heard he was blind and thought he could not resist; suddenly they saw him in person on the field, bending the bow and loosing arrows; they were alarmed together, feared him, and withdrew.
idiomatic: The bandits had heard he was blind and thought him helpless; then they saw him in the battle line, bending the bow and loosing shafts. They stared in shock, feared him, and broke off.

literal: At the time Mu Tipo still hated him without end and wished the city to fall to the bandits; though he knew the danger was acute, he sent no rescue.
idiomatic: Mu Tipo still hated him without end and wished the city would fall to the bandits. Though he knew the peril was acute, he sent no rescue.

literal: Ting fought and held for more than ten days; the bandits at last fled; the city was preserved in the end.
idiomatic: Ting fought and held for more than ten days. The bandits at last fled, and the city stood.

literal: He died in the province.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: His son Junxin ranged widely in books and histories and mastered many miscellaneous arts.
idiomatic: His son Junxin ranged widely in books and histories and mastered many miscellaneous arts.

literal: He held the concurrent posts of regular attendant of the unimpeded staff, deputy envoy on the mission to Chen, and langzhong in the secretariat.
idiomatic: He held concurrent posts as regular attendant of the unimpeded staff, deputy envoy on the mission to Chen, and secretariat langzhong.

literal: When Ting went out, Junxin was also dismissed.
idiomatic: When Ting fell, Junxin was dismissed as well.

literal: Junxin's younger brother Junyan was short in stature and halting in speech, with little talent or learning.
idiomatic: Junxin's younger brother Junyan was short in stature, halting in speech, and slight in talent.

literal: In the Daye era of Sui he rose to clerk of Dongping commandery.
idiomatic: In Sui's Daye era he rose to clerk of Dongping commandery.

literal: When the commandery fell to Zhai Rang, he was taken by Li Mi, who treated him with great courtesy and appointed him recorder; military documents and urgent dispatches were all written by his hand.
idiomatic: When the commandery fell to Zhai Rang, Li Mi took him, treated him with great courtesy, and made him recorder; military documents and urgent dispatches all passed through his hand.

literal: When Mi was defeated, he was killed by Wang Shichong.
idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, Wang Shichong killed him.

literal: Ting's younger brother Xiaoyin had literary talent and was known early.
idiomatic: Ting's younger brother Xiaoyin had literary gifts and was known early.

literal: Though his compositions did not match his elder brother's, he was also quick-witted and eloquent, and understood music.
idiomatic: His compositions did not match his brother's, yet he was quick-witted and eloquent and understood music.

literal: At the end of Wei he was regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and received the Liang envoy.
idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and received the Liang envoy.

literal: At the time Xu Junfang and Yu Xin came on embassy; their fame was very high; the Wei court, hearing of it, held them in weight; those who met them mostly took the outstanding men of the day — men such as Lu Yuanjing all stepped down a rank to assist in office, taking turns as masters of reception.
idiomatic: Xu Junfang and Yu Xin came on embassy then, men of towering fame. The Wei court, hearing of them, treated the occasion with gravity and chose the day's finest to meet them — Lu Yuanjing and others all stepped down a rank to assist, taking turns as masters of reception.

literal: Xiaoyin, young among them, won praise in public discussion.
idiomatic: Xiaoyin, still young among them, won praise in public discussion.

literal: Xiaoyin's younger cousin Mao had considerable gift for words, but loved wine and was frank by nature, and was not held in weight by the age.
idiomatic: Xiaoyin's cousin Mao had a gift for words but loved wine and was blunt by nature, and the age did not esteem him.

literal: In the Daning era he was recommended by his native district for classical learning, made gentleman attendant, declined on grounds of illness, and never again took office.
idiomatic: In the Daning era his native district recommended him for classical learning; he was made gentleman attendant, declined on grounds of illness, and never served again.

literal: When Ting received a weighty commission, he therefore had Mao summoned; Mao could not refuse and came for a time to join him.
idiomatic: When Ting received a weighty commission he summoned Mao; Mao could not refuse and came for a time.

literal: Ting wished to memorialize and give him an office; Mao then fled away.
idiomatic: Ting meant to memorialize and give him an office; Mao fled.

literal: Ting's clansman younger brother Chongru was versed in learning and had literary polish; in youth he was known for practical ability.
idiomatic: Ting's clansman Chongru was versed in learning and had literary polish; in youth he was known for practical ability.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was vice governor of Si Province and regular attendant.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was vice governor of Si Province and regular attendant.

literal: On entering Zhou he was governor of Rongchang commandery.
idiomatic: After Zhou took the realm he was governor of Rongchang commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui he ended as chief administrator of Dang Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he ended as chief administrator of Dang Province.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
